ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, fold a rectangular strip $ABCD$ along $EF$. If $\angle 1=65^\circ$, what is the measure of $\angle AEG$ in degrees?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $AD \parallel BC$,

$\therefore \angle DEF = \angle 1 = 65^\circ$,

By the property of folding, $\angle DEF = \angle DEF = 65^\circ$,

$\therefore \angle AEG = 180^\circ - 2\times65^\circ = \boxed{50^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a rectangular paper strip ABCD. A, E, D are on the same straight line on the upper side, and B, F, C are on the same straight line on the lower side; therefore the upper side AD is parallel to the lower side BC. The crease is the line segment EF from E to F. After folding, the originally upper-right side ED is mapped to the oblique side EG starting from E and passing through G. In the figure, ∠1 is marked near F, and is the angle formed by EF and the lower side BC, known to be 65°. Reasoning: Because AD ∥ BC, and ∠1 is the angle formed by EF and BC, the corresponding angle ∠DEF formed by EF and ED on the parallel line AD is also equal to 65°. The folding is carried out along EF; folding preserves angles unchanged and reflects ED to EG, so ∠GEF = ∠DEF = 65°. Also because A, E, D are on the same straight line, at point E, the three adjacent angles ∠AEG, ∠GEF, and ∠FED form a straight angle of 180°. Therefore ∠AEG = 180° - 65° - 65° = 50°.
